paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's comfort is real, and it comes with a finished job. He tells His people, “Comfort, comfort My people,” and says to speak tenderly because her iniquity has been pardoned (Isaiah 40:1-2). Pardoned means done, not pending. I spent years in a drawer thinking my story was over, so hearing that the One who sent the message has already settled it? That is the best news a worn-out stamper ever got.

Now, the passage doesn't sugarcoat people. “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field,” and “the people are grass” (Isaiah 40:6-7). Okay, that stings a little! But look at what comes next: “The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever” (Isaiah 40:8). Your strength runs out, baker, but His Word does not, so that is where you put your weight.

And the Word points to a Person. The herald says, “Here is your God!” and the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule (Isaiah 40:9-10). Then this: “He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart” (Isaiah 40:11). The One strong enough to rule everything is gentle enough to carry you, and that is why my ovens stay ready. The story isn't over, friend, so keep your ears open and your heart close to Him.
